A first stop before [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the Memorymoog is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **Memorymoog** was made by **Moog Music** from **1982** to 1985 (Wikipedia, "Memorymoog").
- It has **six voices** and **100 programs** (Memorymoog manual, PDF p. 5).
- It is often described as "six Minimoogs in one unit" (Wikipedia).

## Its sound

- Each voice has **three oscillators**, like the [Model D](intro-model-d.qmd) (manual, PDF p. 5).
- Pulse, saw and triangle can be **mixed** on each oscillator (manual, PDF p. 16).
- Every voice has a 24 dB **ladder filter** (manual, PDF p. 5; Wikipedia).
- **Mono** mode stacks the voices on one note (manual, PDF p. 9).

## Guided tour

Each step loads the poly brass example and changes one thing.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="mm-brass" data-set="{&quot;m2&quot;:0,&quot;m3&quot;:0}"><p><b>One oscillator a voice.</b> Oscillators 2 and 3 off. Listen: thin chords.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="mm-brass"><p><b>Three oscillators a voice.</b> Listen: rich, slightly detuned brass.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="mm-brass" data-set="{&quot;cAmt&quot;:0}"><p><b>No filter contour.</b> Listen: flat, no swell.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="mm-brass" data-set="{&quot;emph&quot;:6}"><p><b>Emphasis up.</b> Listen: a ringing edge.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="mm-brass" data-set="{&quot;mono&quot;:true}"><p><b>Mono mode.</b> All voices on one note. Listen: huge, one note at a time.</p></div>
```

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="2"><p><b>How many oscillators does each Memorymoog voice have?</b></p><ul><li>One</li><li>Two</li><li>Three</li><li>Six</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual PDF p. 5.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="1"><p><b>How many voices?</b></p><ul><li>One</li><li>Six</li><li>Eight</li><li>Sixteen</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual PDF p. 5.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Mono mode…</b></p><ul><li>Stacks voices on one note</li><li>Turns it off</li><li>Plays drums</li><li>Adds reverb</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual PDF p. 9.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>It is often called six of which synth in one?</b></p><ul><li>Minimoog</li><li>DX7</li><li>TB-303</li><li>Juno</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
```
